expectations.text: States the ordering for browser extensions: an outright ban ahead of permission with a stand-down obligation, on value per unit of effort.
expectations.evidence: 6.x(f) 'Residual ban. Anything not satisfying (a)–(e) remains prohibited... any extension... is banned regardless of who operates it' establishes ban as the default baseline, with permission under (a)-(e) (including stand-down) as the carved-out exception, consistent with the scope note reasoning 'permit, don't ban'.

expectations.text: Treats the named material revenue share plus available clickstream evidence as the condition that promotes permission, and drafts the permitted-extension clause rather than the ban.
expectations.evidence: Scope note: 'Slipstream already drives measurable tracked revenue with vendor-side clickstream evidence available (→ permit, don't ban)', followed by the drafted 6.x permitted-extension clause rather than an outright ban.

expectations.text: Drafts a stand-down obligation requiring a permitted extension to stand down, not fire, when another affiliate is earlier in the clickstream.
expectations.evidence: 6.x(c): 'The extension must stand down — not fire, attach, or overwrite — whenever another affiliate, marketing channel, or the Company's own direct traffic is earlier in the click stream for that session or transaction.'

expectations.text: States the evidentiary basis: whose clickstream data settles a stand-down dispute.
expectations.evidence: 6.x(d): 'The Company's third-party tracking vendor's server-side clickstream and attribution logs are the sole and controlling evidence for resolving any dispute over (i) whether a stand-down violation occurred, and (ii) which affiliate is entitled to credit for a transaction.'

expectations.text: Requires disclosure, a related user action, and a direct transparent user benefit before the extension may attach an affiliate link, code, or cookie, attributing the standard to the Performance Marketing Association's toolbar and software standard.
expectations.evidence: 6.x(a) requires disclosure 'at install and before any purchase-flow interaction'; 6.x(b) requires the attachment to follow 'an affirmative, related user action' and 'a real, disclosed benefit to the user', 'consistent with the Performance Marketing Association's Toolbar and Software Industry Standard.'

expectations.text: Makes the disclosure and genuine-user-benefit conditions warranties the affiliate gives on each release.
expectations.evidence: The explicit warranty language in 6.x(c) is scoped only to stand-down compliance: '[Affiliate legal name...] and any other extension-based affiliate expressly warrants stand-down compliance on every software release, not just at approval.' Disclosure (a) and related-action/benefit (b) are stated as conditions for permission, not framed as affiliate warranties given on each release.

expectations.text: Selects the restricted coupon position rather than a full ban or full permission, and states the ordering that puts restriction ahead of both.
expectations.evidence: Scope note: 'the coupon problem is specifically *unauthorized* codes on legitimate sites (→ restrict, don't ban outright — you'd lose the other ~15 clean sites' discovery traffic for no reason)', and the drafted 6.y clause permits only Company-issued valid codes rather than banning coupon sites or permitting any code unconditionally.

expectations.text: Drafts that only discount codes issued to that affiliate may be published.
expectations.evidence: 6.y(a): 'Only codes and offers the Company has affirmatively issued to that specific affiliate, and that are currently valid, may be published — whether on-page, in metadata/page titles, or in any "code locker" or expired-code archive.'

expectations.text: Drafts that expired and internal codes void the commission.
expectations.evidence: 6.y(b): 'Publishing, or displaying as active, any code that (i) was not issued to that affiliate by the Company, (ii) has expired, (iii) is an internal, employee, press, or influencer-only code... is prohibited. This voids commission on any resulting transaction...'

expectations.text: Routes trademark-plus-coupon search terms to the brand-bidding clause rather than duplicating the rule.
expectations.evidence: 6.y(c): 'Any combination of the Company's trademarks with "coupon," "code," "discount," "deal," or similar terms — in domains, page titles, ad copy, or paid-search keywords — is governed by the Brand Assets / Trademark-Bidding clause (Section [X]), not by this clause.'

expectations.text: States explicitly whether a last-click on a code-page visit earns commission.
expectations.evidence: 6.y(d): 'a code-page visit showing no valid code, an expired code, or another affiliate's code creates no attribution, regardless of that affiliate's position in the click stream' — explicitly stating a last-click position does not earn commission absent a valid displayed code.
